A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CULTIVate benchmark and AHEaD framework. Text extraction and visual inspection support comparison of the main text and complete appendices, including corresponding equations, tables, figures and prompts despite renumbering and substantial rewriting.

before.justification: V1 reports original evaluations of six image generators, human judgments, metric correlations and descriptor-generation ablations in the main text and appendix.

after.justification: V2 retains original benchmark results and reports expanded human evaluation, additional metric comparisons, descriptor-coverage assessments and image-editing examples.

M1.justification: The proposer–refiner and descriptor-matching framework remains. Equation 4 now clips negative exaggeration deviations at zero. Appendix A.5, Figure 8 and Table 32 also introduce a concrete procedure for converting descriptor feedback into Nano Banana editing instructions, extending the previously suggested application.

E1.justification: The 16-country, 576-prompt, nine-category generation benchmark is retained. Human validation expands from seven to eleven countries, and Figure 8 adds a small qualitative image-editing task using four existing cultural activities.

E2.justification: V2 adds GPT-4o-as-judge and GPT-4o-based VIEScore to Table 2; GPT-4o also joins the per-generator comparison in Table 6. The earlier ITA, CuRe and InternVL/Qwen judge comparators remain. Nano Banana becoming Gemini 2.5 Flash Image is a naming change.

E3.justification: Human evaluation increases from 216 to 398 forms, with activity sampling changing from one to one–two activities per category. V2 additionally evaluates AHEaD using Qwen2.5-VL, with its own calibrated threshold, enabling comparisons against judges using the same backbone. These substantially extend the validation design; generation counts and seeds remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 expands component analysis across two backbones and adds descriptor-completeness assessments, country/activity exaggeration diagnostics and four feedback-guided editing case studies. The original proposer–refiner and threshold ablations are retained as Tables 4–5, and the descriptor-source experiment remains Table 10; these are not new analyses.

E5.justification: V2 adds ± quantities in Table 1, human-rating standard deviations in Table 13, Krippendorff’s alpha and Cohen’s kappa in Appendix A.4, and a p≤0.0001 statement in Table 3. Table 1 does not explain its ± quantities and leaves FAITH/SDIV uncertainties as placeholders. Additional random-seed runs are not established.

E6.justification: Many reported values change: Table 1’s Qwen HAL scores for GN/GS move from 0.53/0.59 to 0.51/0.56. Overall FAITH correlation changes from 0.38 to 0.47 under expanded human evaluation, so this is not a same-setting gain. V2 additionally reports Qwen-backed FAITH at 0.42, GPT-4o judging at 0.48, VIEScore at 0.35, and new coverage/editing findings.

T1.justification: Equation 4 changes EXAG from a maximum raw deviation for one image to an average of nonnegative maximum deviations across images, altering the formal metric definition. The bipartite-graph and indicator notation otherwise restates existing descriptor matching; no substantial theorem or proof development is added.

C1.justification: The benchmark, descriptor-based evaluation and Global North bias claims persist. The headline correlation advantage changes from 7% in v1 to 27% in v2, explicitly emphasizing FAITH against matched-backbone MLLM judges. Table 2 supports an absolute correlation difference of 0.27 (0.47 versus 0.20), not a 27% relative increase.

C2.justification: V2 acknowledges that direct descriptor recall cannot be measured without ground truth, explains the interpretability/performance tradeoff between ITA-based and MLLM-based exaggeration scoring, and hypothesizes why annotator agreement differs by region. The existing Appendix A.2 discussion of LLM and reference-image bias remains essentially unchanged.

D1.justification: V2 supplies previously missing VQAScore and CuRe configurations, explicit per-dimension averaging, Qwen model/threshold details, L40S hardware information, and EXAG-candidate and editing prompts. It adds a project-page link and revises existing prompt schemas, including removing the necessity field. These documentation changes do not establish that earlier experiments were rerun.

R1.justification: V2 adds OpenBias as methodological inspiration, VIEScore, additional compositional-understanding studies and statistical-reliability references; Culture-TRIP and Liu et al.’s cultural-gap paper disappear. The central positioning around social activities and descriptor-based faithfulness evaluation remains. Several other citation changes merely update publication metadata.

P1.justification: The abstract, much of the introduction, related work, methodology and experimental narrative are extensively rewritten. V2 adds Section 4.3, reorganizes related-work categories, expands appendix explanations and rewrites prompt documentation. This constitutes substantial editorial restructuring beyond the added scientific content.

P2.justification: V2 redraws Figure 2, enlarges Figure 4 into two rows, restructures comparisons by backbone and separates component results into Table 3. It adds Figure 8 and diagnostic/human-score tables. Appendix prompts are reformatted into wrapped, readable blocks, replacing v1’s small monospaced blocks with overflowing lines.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens the central metric-validation evidence through a second backbone, stronger judges, broader human assessment and explicit agreement analysis, addressing v1’s narrower validation. More complete implementation details and readable appendix prompts improve reproducibility. Undefined uncertainty entries and the misleading percentage wording remain, but do not outweigh these substantial gains.
